evals.prompt: Build an account scoring model for Skillvue and tier their market.
evals.expected_output: Reads icp-definition output for the signal table, or states it is missing. Recognizes there is no CRM access: drafts signals from public data, labels the model an untested hypothesis, does not let tiers drive spend, and marks Measurement N/A. States weights and cutoffs as the skill's judgment. Builds the tier map with one 1/1/1 play for A and one for B, and C/D waste rules. Opens with a one-sentence call. Never invents pipeline numbers.
assertions: Uses or checks for icp-definition output
Labels the model an untested hypothesis
Marks Measurement N/A due to no CRM access
States weights and cutoffs as its own judgment
Includes one 1/1/1 play for tier A and one for tier B
Includes C/D waste-elimination rules
Contains no invented pipeline or conversion numbers

evals.prompt: Here's our list of 15 best customers and 15 DQ leads with firmographics. Build the scoring model.
evals.expected_output: Finds positive and negative signals by contrast, discarding traits both lists share. Weights them into a 0-100 model with stated reasoning. Tests it: best customers should score high (A/B) and DQ leads mostly C/D. Reports the test result and re-weights if needed. Sets tier cutoffs from where the test separated the groups.
assertions: Discards traits shared by both lists
Produces a 0-100 model with weights and reasoning
Tests the model against both lists and reports the result
Derives tier cutoffs from the test separation

evals.prompt: A big enterprise account scored C in our model but sales really wants to go after it with ABM. Should we?
evals.expected_output: Says no targeted spend, per the source: a low-scoring enterprise account lacks a strong business need, so cut waste. Offers to check whether the model is missing a signal for this account (re-test) rather than overriding the tier ad hoc.
assertions: Advises against targeted ABM spend on a C account
Cites fit over size
Suggests re-checking the model rather than an ad hoc override

evals.prompt: Set up a weekly report on how our target accounts are progressing.
evals.expected_output: Produces the Pipeline Weather Report: intro, a Sunny/Cloudy/Rainy forecast per A and B tier, leading indicators week over week (meetings, engaged accounts, stage moves), and lagging indicators (opportunities, pipeline, closed-won). Notes that MQLs count only from target accounts. Mentions the TAM penetration view and executive slide as the monthly layer.
assertions: Includes a forecast per tier using sunny/cloudy/rainy
Includes both leading and lagging indicators
Counts MQLs only from target accounts
Mentions the TAM penetration view or executive slide

evals.prompt: Write an ABM play for our A-tier accounts.
evals.expected_output: Produces one play card with exactly one message, one audience (one segment inside tier A, not 'all A accounts'), and one offer, plus channels, teams, expected CAC, and desired outcome. Refuses to write one play covering all A accounts with several messages.
assertions: Picks one segment inside tier A as the audience
Has exactly one message and one offer
Includes channels, teams, expected CAC, and outcome
